items.title: feat(wallet): optional paymaster for registration and trading fees
items.body:
Hi guys, I was experimenting with vulcan cli for backtesting and thought a feature for setting fee-payers for opening/closing/registering traders would be helpful, feel free to decline however if it is not.

## Summary

Adds an optional paymaster: a stored sponsor wallet that pays Solana fees and RegisterTrader rent while the trader wallet still signs. A zero-SOL trader wallet can register, deposit, trade, close, and withdraw; the sponsor gains no authority over funds or positions. Nothing changes unless a paymaster is linked or `--fee-payer` is passed.

## Changes

- `vulcan wallet set-fee-payer <WALLET>` / `clear-fee-payer` link and unlink the paymaster; `wallet list` shows it. Global `--fee-payer <WALLET>` overrides it for one command.
- MCP: `vulcan_wallet_set_fee_payer` / `vulcan_wallet_clear_fee_payer`; the link is read at each transaction so it applies to the next call in a running session.
- The sponsor is injected into the existing signing paths (`send_or_dry_run` for trade/margin/position/subaccount actions, the onboarding signer for registration): sponsor becomes fee payer, trader signs first, sponsor second. Original single-signer code paths are untouched.
- Fail-fast checks: unknown sponsor → `FEE_PAYER_WALLET_NOT_FOUND` before any RPC call (also in `--dry-run`); underfunded sponsor → `INSUFFICIENT_SOL_FOR_FEE` with balance and fee in the message. A sponsor equal to the trader is ignored.
- Error catalog entries, tool catalog regenerated, onboarding skill / CONTEXT.md / README updated.

## User Impact

Default flows are unchanged: one extra local file check per transaction, same fee payer, same signature, same JSON output (`fee_payer` fields appear only when set). One new global flag, two new `wallet` subcommands, two new MCP tools.

## Validation

- `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test` (234 unit + 11 integration, including the tool catalog drift check and a structural test that every transaction-submitting module routes through the paymaster-aware helpers)
- Sponsored registration verified live on mainnet: a fresh zero-SOL trader wallet registered and onboarded with a sponsor paying; `vulcan status` reports registered
- Not yet verified live: a sponsored deposit / order / close

items.title: feat(wallet): paymaster that pays fees for registration and trading
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a **paymaster**: a stored sponsor wallet that pays Solana fees and RegisterTrader rent for every Vulcan transaction, while the trader wallet still signs. A zero-SOL trader wallet can register, deposit, trade, close, and withdraw; the sponsor gains no authority over funds or positions.

- `vulcan wallet set-fee-payer <WALLET>` / `clear-fee-payer` link and unlink the paymaster; `wallet list` shows it. Global `--fee-payer <WALLET>` overrides it for one command.
- MCP: `vulcan_wallet_set_fee_payer` / `vulcan_wallet_clear_fee_payer`; the link is read at each transaction, so it applies to the next call in a running session.
- One linked paymaster serves every trader wallet (`-w`, `set-default`, MCP session wallet). Naming the trader itself as sponsor is a no-op.
- All transactions go through the shared send helper (trade, margin, position, subaccount) or the onboarding signer (registration); both build the tx with the sponsor as fee payer and sign trader-then-sponsor.
- Fail-fast checks: unknown sponsor → `FEE_PAYER_WALLET_NOT_FOUND` before any RPC call (also in `--dry-run`); underfunded sponsor → `INSUFFICIENT_SOL_FOR_FEE` with balance and fee in the message.

## Impact on existing flows

**None unless a paymaster is linked or `--fee-payer` is passed.**

- Default path: the send helper performs one extra local file check (is a paymaster linked?) per transaction, then behaves as before — trader is fee payer, single signature, no extra RPC calls. Registration is unchanged when no sponsor resolves.
- JSON output: `wallet list` and `account register` gain a `fee_payer` field **only when set** (verified absent otherwise). No existing fields change.
- CLI: one new global flag, two new `wallet` subcommands. MCP: two new tools; existing tool schemas unchanged (`vulcan_wallet_list` description mentions the optional field).
- Error surface: new catalog codes listed above. A linked sponsor whose wallet file was later removed is ignored rather than failing.
- Internal: `AppContext::new` takes a `fee_payer_override` argument (three call sites updated). `send_or_dry_run*` signatures unchanged; the sponsor signature is injected into the existing signing block, the original single-signer path and its `PARTIAL_SIGNATURE` check are untouched.
- All 228 pre-existing unit tests and 5 pre-existing integration tests pass unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test` (234 unit + 11 integration, tool catalog drift check)
- [x] Unit: sponsored registration signing accumulates trader + sponsor and rejects a missing sponsor; resolver precedence (explicit > flag > linked > none, live re-read); fee-check amounts in message; structural guard that every tx-submitting module routes through the paymaster-aware helpers
- [x] CLI integration (hermetic, closed RPC port): unknown sponsor fails before network; same-as-trader is a no-op; valid sponsor reaches RPC; `set-fee-payer` / `clear-fee-payer` round trip; global flag overrides the link
- [x] MCP stdio session: set → list shows link → clear → link gone → unknown wallet rejected
- [x] `cargo test --test cli_integration -- --ignored`: dry-run sponsored registration against live RPC reports the sponsor pubkey
- [x] Unsponsored path verified live: reaches the SOL rent preflight and fails with `INSUFFICIENT_SOL_FOR_REGISTRATION` on an empty wallet
- [x] Sponsored registration verified live on mainnet: a fresh zero-SOL trader wallet registered and onboarded with a sponsor wallet paying; transaction finalized and `vulcan status` reports registered
- [ ] Sponsored trade verified live (deposit / order / close with the linked paymaster paying)

items.title: Support a fallback RPC endpoint (single RPC_URL is a paymaster SPOF)
items.body:
Kora accepts exactly one `RPC_URL`. When that provider degrades (2026-09-02: Helius mainnet account-data methods returned 500s for an extended window while `getHealth` passed), the paymaster has no way to keep operating — balance checks fail (see companion issue on gauge conflation) and, with real traffic, fee estimation/submission would fail too. The only remediation is a manual secret swap plus a revision roll.

Proposed: accept an ordered list of RPC endpoints (`RPC_URLS`) with per-request failover on 5xx/transport errors and a simple health-based preference for the primary — same shape as typical Solana client failover. Even a minimal two-endpoint failover removes the paymaster's single point of failure on third-party RPC.

Context: SDP runs kora-mainnet-int / kora-devnet-int on Cloud Run with the RPC URL injected from Secret Manager; a config change requires a new revision, so provider incidents currently mean paged humans and manual rotation.

items.title: Per-call paymasterToken override drops configured transferMaxFee
items.body:
## Problem

`transfer()` reads `paymasterToken` and `transferMaxFee` with `config ?? this._config`. A non-nullish second argument that omits `transferMaxFee` drops the account cap. `{ paymasterToken }` only is enough.

README lists those two as independent optional per-call overrides. EVM 4337, 7702-gasless, and solana-gasless merge per-call config onto the account config.

No second argument still applies the cap. Passing both fields still applies it. The Jetton send is already bound to the original transfer (#48 / #51). What this skips is the commission ceiling: a high `gaslessEstimate` commission is signed and paid in the paymaster token.

## Proposed fix

Merge per-call config onto the account config (`{ ...this._config, ...config }`) so omitting `transferMaxFee` keeps the account cap.

Add a test: account `transferMaxFee` below the quoted commission, `transfer(..., { paymasterToken })` only — must throw and must not send.

items.title: WDK Track 2: gasless transactions (USD₮ as gas token)
items.body:
## Summary

Explore/implement **Track 2 (Gasless) of the Aleph Hackathon 2026 WDK track** — $500 USDt for "best project leveraging WDK's gasless wallet modules." Currently out of scope for the CLI-track integration ([Track 1](https://hacki.crecimiento.build/h/aleph-hackathon-2026/tracks/wdk-track), the one we're actually pursuing today) — tracked separately here as a stretch goal / future work.

## Track requirements (from the [WDK track page](https://hacki.crecimiento.build/h/aleph-hackathon-2026/tracks/wdk-track))

- Core dependency: `@tetherto/wdk`
- At least one gasless module: Solana, EVM 7702, ERC-4337, TON, or TRON
- USD₮ used as the gas token
- Node.js 22.18.0+
- Judged on: real user problem resolution, working end-to-end demo, *meaningful* WDK integration (not a superficial wrapper), UX usability for non-crypto users or AI agents
- Submission needs: public repo + README detailing WDK modules used, direct GitHub permalinks to the integration code, an async demo video, a package list with versions, `.env.example`, network/token deployment details
- **Testnet USD₮ is only available on Sepolia** (via Candide and Pimlico) — our contracts are currently deployed to **Base Sepolia**, a different network. Other chains require deploying a mock token.

## Why this is separate from today's Track 1 work

Given the submission deadline (23 Aug 2026, 12:00 ART) landed a few hours after this was scoped, going for gasless on top of the CLI integration risked a half-wired, untested paymaster setup on a chain (Base Sepolia) the gasless track doesn't officially support with testnet USDT. Track 1 ($1,000, CLI/MCP) was prioritized as the safer, fully-functional bet.

## What gasless integration would require

- [ ] Decide: migrate to Ethereum Sepolia (to get real testnet USD₮ via Candide/Pimlico) vs. deploy `MockUSDT` as the gas token on Base Sepolia and self-host the paymaster config
- [ ] Add `@tetherto/wdk` + the chosen gasless module as dependencies
- [ ] Wire a paymaster (Candide or Pimlico) so USD₮ pays gas instead of ETH
- [ ] Update frontend wallet flow (`web/src/app/providers.tsx`, `web/src/lib/wagmi.ts`) or add a parallel WDK-gasless path for at least one write flow (`buyPolicy` is the natural candidate — smallest, most user-facing transaction)
- [ ] Document exact package versions, setup, and `.env.example` additions per submission requirements
- [ ] Record/update the demo video to show a gasless transaction (buyer pays premium without holding ETH for gas)

## Documentation links

- Track page: https://hacki.crecimiento.build/h/aleph-hackathon-2026/tracks/wdk-track
- WDK docs home: https://docs.wdk.tether.io
- Core module: https://docs.wdk.tether.io/sdk/core-module
- Core module — configuration: https://docs.wdk.tether.io/sdk/core-module/configuration/
- Core module — API reference: https://docs.wdk.tether.io/sdk/core-module/api-reference/
- Core module — usage: https://docs.wdk.tether.io/sdk/core-module/usage/

- **EVM gasless — EIP-7702**: https://docs.wdk.tether.io/sdk/wallet-modules/wallet-evm-7702-gasless/
- **EVM gasless — ERC-4337 (smart accounts)**: https://docs.wdk.tether.io/sdk/wallet-modules/wallet-evm-erc-4337/

## Packages referenced

items.title: Use provided Privy policy ID as default sponsorship fallback
items.body:
### Motivation
- Ensure a deterministic paymaster policy id is always supplied so UserOperations are not sent without an effective paymaster when env vars are missing.
- Improve runtime compatibility across Privy/SDK versions that expect different paymaster context shapes (`sponsorshipPolicyId` vs `policyId`).
- Avoid spurious Solana connector warnings in apps that only use Polygon smart wallets.

### Description
- Add `DEFAULT_PRIVY_SPONSORSHIP_POLICY_ID = 'tza7scd2d4q8v11ptrhozp5r'` and use it as a fallback when resolving `sponsorshipPolicyId` in both `BilleteraApp` and `Home` scopes.
- Construct `sponsorshipContext` to include both `sponsorshipPolicyId` and `policyId` for compatibility and wire it into `SmartWalletsProvider` via `config.paymasterContext`.
- Keep the per-transaction explicit `paymasterContext` on `client.sendTransaction` and preserve the AA21/prefund error handling that retries once with the minimal `{ policyId }` shape.
- Remove the hard guard that blocked sending when the env var was absent (now unnecessary because of the provided default), and add `loginMethods: ['email']` to silence Solana connector warnings.

### Testing

items.title: [Epic] Solana money-path hardening (recipient guards, swap-path signing, MAX reserve, Token-2022)
items.body:
## Epic: Solana money-path hardening

Per-chain hardening initiative (XRP model: #979). Deep-dive survey 2026-08-23 across SDK/iOS/Android/Windows; all S1 items re-verified against source. ALL-PLATFORM rule applies.

### S1 — money loss
1. **No off-curve recipient guard.** Address validation is bare WalletCore base58 on all platforms (`vultisig-windows/core/ui/vault/send/form/validateSendForm.ts:40`); a pasted ATA/PDA passes, and an SPL send then creates an ATA-of-an-ATA nobody controls. iOS/Android ship `isOnCurve` (SolanaProgramDerivedAddress) but use it only for derivation.
2. **Burn/program-address guard missing from the wallet send path.** `assertSafeDestination` (knows the Solana burn/program addresses, `packages/core/chain/security/dangerousAddresses.ts:43-49`) is wired into `prepareSendTxFromKeys` (agent/CLI path) but never called from `buildSendKeysignPayload` (`packages/core/mpc/keysign/send/build.ts:41-100`) — the function every wallet UI calls.
3. **Aggregator swaps use the WalletCore decode→re-encode documented unsafe for v0+ALT.** All 4 platforms overwrite `recentBlockhash` and re-encode (`signingInputs/resolvers/solana/index.ts:75-100`; android's own warning at `SolanaSignatureEnvelope.kt:55-63`). #1204 fixed this for dApp raw txs by signing verbatim; swaps never got the treatment.
4. **LiFi/SwapKit Solana swaps have no instruction guard** — allow-list runs only for `provider==='jupiter'` (#1356); LiFi's EVM branch gets router guards, its Solana branch gets nothing.
5. **iOS never security-scans a Solana swap** (scanner factory: `.EVM` or throw → swallowed to `.idle`) — tracked on iOS, listed here for the epic picture.

### S2 (ordered)
- No rent-exempt reserve (890880 lamports) on wallet MAX send — appears in zero repos; guard already exists for staking (`useSolanaRentReserveQuery.ts`) and Kamino (iOS `KaminoTransactionPreparer.swift:261`)
- Send amount never reconciled against the fee actually encoded (#1586); deposit path does it right (`deposit/keysignPayload/build.ts:836-841`)
- Blockhash: Win send never refreshes (deposit refreshes every 20s); Android refresh is a no-op for signSolana flows
- No rebroadcast-until-confirmed loop; `lastValidBlockHeight` never plumbed → expired txs poll pending forever
- False-success at sub-finalized commitment (iOS err-check only in finalized branch; Android dup-verify ignores err)
- Token-2022: zero extension handling (#1728) — transfer-fee mints silently deliver less than displayed; ATA rent constant assumes legacy 165B account
- Extension ALT resolution fails open (`inpage-provider/.../solana/utils/index.ts:11-27`); SDK's own resolver fails closed
- No fee-payer/signer-0 vault check on dApp raw txs; multi-tx requests blind-signed uncapped
- Golden vectors don't exercise the production encoder shape (no v0Msg/priority fields; no CreateAndTransferToken or Token-2022 vector) — #1585 branch exists

### Roadmap-bucket (separate)
Gasless (relayer/paymaster — VultiServer candidate), spam/verification labels + ML hide, address-poisoning defense in history, durable-nonce story (MPC-natural: no blockhash expiry mid-ceremony).

items.title: feat(nodejs-server-wallets): Dynamic native gas sponsorship, Solana support, idempotent transfers
items.body:
Replaces ZeroDev/Pimlico with Dynamic's native gas sponsorship, adds Solana
alongside EVM, and adds retry-safe (idempotent) transfers.

## Gas sponsorship

- **EVM** — EIP-7702 delegation to Dynamic's UGD contract plus an EIP-712
  `AuthorizedExecutions` intent, relayed by Dynamic. No bundler, paymaster, or
  smart account.
- **SVM** — fee-payer replacement. Sponsorship must precede signing (swapping the
  fee payer changes the message), and your server broadcasts rather than a relayer.
- Delegated wallets on both chains, plus a sign-here/relay-there split: signing
  needs the delegated credentials, relaying needs only the environment API token.

## Structure

`src/evm/` and `src/svm/` mirror each other. Chain-specific library code is
`lib/<feature>/<chain>.ts` and the two chains never import each other; unsuffixed
`lib/` modules are chain-agnostic. Chain dispatch uses exhaustiveness-checked
switches, so adding a chain fails the build at every site that needs work.

## Idempotency

`lib/transfer/` presents one call shape for either chain — native or token, server
or delegated signer — and picks the right retry mechanism underneath.
`src/examples/idempotency/` shows each mechanism in isolation. `IDEMPOTENCY.md`
documents both with measurements.

**The two chains need opposite handling, and this is the part worth reviewing.**
EVM derives the intent nonce from a business key, and the delegate contract's
unordered bitmap admits it exactly once per wallet. On SVM the transaction id is
`signatures[0]` — the fee payer's, which under sponsorship is Dynamic's sponsor —
so re-signing the wallet's signature is deduped by Solana, and it is *rebuilding*
with a fresh blockhash that yields a second executable transaction. The safe retry
unit there is the signed bytes: sign once, persist, rebroadcast verbatim.

## Try it

```bash
cd examples/nodejs-server-wallets
cp .example.env .env   # add DYNAMIC_API_TOKEN + DYNAMIC_ENVIRONMENT_ID
pnpm install

pnpm smoke             # offline: type-check + argument validation
pnpm smoke --all       # + signing and sponsored transactions (spends relayer budget)
```

Requires EVM/SVM Gas Sponsorship enabled for the environment.

## Also

- `@dynamic-labs-wallet/{node,node-evm,node-svm}` → 1.0.105; unused deps dropped;
  all versions pinned exactly.
- `pnpm smoke` — tiered runner (offline / signing / onchain) over the real CLI
  entrypoints, so expensive tiers are opt-in.
- Per-directory READMEs and a project tree in the root README.

items.title: Locked vaults, creators proof page, and a plain-language home page
items.body:
## Summary

**Locked vaults (contracts).** Immutable contracts under `ethereum/contracts/locks/`: one `LockedVault` per lock that holds any ERC20 or the native coin and releases everything to its owner once its rule is met; a CREATE2 `LockedVaultFactory` that is also the registry of verified conditions; and `Date`, `Price` (Chainlink), `AllOf`, `AnyOf` conditions. Every lock has a hard deadline (max 10 years) so a broken feed can delay funds but never strand them. No owner or admin functions, no upgrade path, nothing registered in `SavingsCore`. Factory address lives in `frontend/src/networkConfig.json` as `lockedVaultFactory`; deploy with `npm run deploy-locks --workspace=ethereum`.

**Locked vaults (frontend).** A "Locked vaults" dashboard section (create on a date or a verified price, deposit listed or custom tokens, release when open), a public proof page at `/lock/:chain/:address` readable without a wallet, and a creators landing page at `/proof-of-lock`. Adapter surface: `supportsLocks`, `getLocks`, `getLock`, `createLock`, `depositToLock`, `releaseLock`.

**Landing.** Home page rewritten for someone new to crypto, targeting "savings account you can't withdraw from". All implementation and security detail moved to a new `/security` page. New static SEO guides for "how to stop impulse buying" and "how to stop impulse shopping"; all guides cross-link, sitemap and Vercel headers updated.

**Docs.** `SECURITY.md` and `GOVERNANCE.md` state locked vaults as the deliberate exception to the exit-right invariant: no bypass, no penalty exit, no upgrade path, so nothing to escape from. CHANGELOG and in-app release notes updated.

## Test plan

- [x] `hardhat test`: 332 passing, 0 failing (19 new in `test/LockedVaults.ts`)
- [x] Frontend suite: 259 passing; the 20 failures are the known Solana-validator baseline
- [x] Production build compiles
- [x] Home, `/security`, `/proof-of-lock` and both new guides checked in headless Chrome
- [ ] Deploy the factory to a local node (`npm run deploy-modular` now does this on localhost) and walk through create → deposit → release with MetaMask
- [ ] Verify the Chainlink feed addresses in `networkConfig.json` for Base and Optimism before a mainnet deploy

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Paymaster allowlist reads the module registry, so lock creation and deposits are not sponsored for passkey users yet.
- Locks do not interact with the account freeze or recovery modules; SECURITY.md says so.
